faq.a: Hossein is associated with the Arabic form حُسَيْن, whose core sense is hossein; diminutive of 'handsome'.

faq.q: What is the origin of Hossein?
faq.a: Hossein is associated with Arabic. Hossein is Arabic حُسَيْن (Ḥusayn), a diminutive of حَسَن, meaning 'handsome, good'. It was borne by the Prophet's grandson.
Yes — the underlying form حُسَيْن is Arabic.
Hossein can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hossein should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ḥusayn is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Hossein mean in Persian?

A romanized syllable approximation is hos-sein. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hossein?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hossein, hossein. Script forms are حسين, حسین, حُسَيْن, हुसैन.

faq.q: Is Hossein a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
